previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for hyponatremia and hyperkalemia detected during a routine outpatient visit. Her electrolyte imbalances were attributed to a combination of torsemide, irbesartan, and sodium bicarbonate. These medications were held during admission, and she received normal saline. Her sodium improved from 123 to 131 and potassium decreased from 6.1 to 4.5. She remained euvolemic and stable. On discharge, irbesartan and sodium bicarbonate were discontinued, torsemide was changed to every other day, and amlodipine was started for blood pressure control. She was advised to continue fluid restriction, monitor daily weights, and follow up with her primary care provider and nephrologist.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking part in your care at ___ 
___. You were admitted because your son and 
niece felt you were more confused at home. There were a few 
bacteria in your urine, so you were initially given antibiotics. 
However, because there was not inflammation, we don't think you 
had a true urinary tract infection. You also were found to have 
decreased kidney function, probably because you had not been 
drinking enough fluids. We think that your confusion was most 
likely related to dehydration. We gave you some fluids and made 
sure you were drinking enough water and other beverages at the 
hospital. Your kidney function has now improved, and is back to 
your baseline. 

We have arranged for you to return home with additional 
services. A visiting nurse and home health aide will come to 
your house to help with medications and monitoring your health. 
A physical therapist can help you stay active and check up on 
your back and leg pain. To make sure you have the right amount 
of fluid in your body, please weigh yourself every morning, and 
call your doctor if weight goes up more than 3 lbs. 

We wish you a safe and healthy return home. 
 
Sincerely,
Your ___ Team
